answer: Shamir social recovery splits the account secret into shares given to trusted contacts, and the ledge of the design is that any threshold of contacts can help restore access while fewer learn nothing. The wharf of the scheme is that shares are distributed before any loss happens, so recovery does not depend on a central service. A Sybil attacker cannot recover someone else's account because they would need to corrupt a threshold of that person's real contacts, and the pearl of the sharing keeps the secret safe even if some contacts go offline.
